correctness.rationale: For every n>=2 and every polytope with exactly the braid normal fan, outward rays are centered indicators of final permutation segments. The strict inward tangent condition equals positivity of all n-1 prefix sums. Under the stated generic subset-sum condition, the n rotations of each labeled permutation have exactly one strict-positive rotation, giving (n-1)! illuminated vertices; perturbation bounds all nongeneric directions. The n specified directions illuminate disjoint complete vertex classes, hence all boundary faces. Counting vertices proves ordinary n; integrating their constraints proves fractional n. All assumptions and endpoints (including n=2) are handled. An exact-integer standalone script independently passed 1,258,632 finite checks of these incidences and weighted-zonotope facets; the infinite claim rests on the analytical argument.

originality.rationale: Searches of a mathematical result index and primary full texts isolate a natural all-dimensional exact illumination statement not implied by the closest prior works. The low-dimensional truncated-octahedron value is already known and acknowledged. The key difference is a generic (n-1)! cone-incidence law preserved by every full braid-fan deformation, yielding both sharp ordinary and fractional n without symmetry. Historical priority could be incomplete due to older fan/illumination work; absence of search results is not treated as proof of novelty.
residual_risks: An obscure prior theorem about the illumination of all braid-fan polytopes or an unpublished cycle-lemma application may have escaped indexing.
The full text of the recent Gorodzha global fractional bound was not accessible; its abstract and stated theorem do not indicate a dominating exact braid-fan calculation.
Prior exact cases in dimension 2 or 3 of the polytope are not new and are excluded from the claimed independent novelty.

value.rationale: Illumination is a natural sharp covering invariant; the family is the entire type cone of the braid normal fan, including polytopes without vertex transitivity. The theorem identifies both ordinary and fractional exact values n despite n! vertices, as well as a uniform sharp (n-1)! one-direction incidence. The fan is a structural hypothesis, not an arbitrary numeric restriction, and the result does not follow from published approximate upper bounds or finite low-dimensional tables. The fan-coarsening boundary marks a mathematically meaningful scope limitation.
